title: The Aftershocks of the LaMelo Trade
contentHtml:
Imagine my surprise last Friday morning when I woke up in my hotel room in Philadelphia and discovered a prominent NBA Twitter personality had tagged me in a tweet lambasting several media members for their years of slander characterizing LaMelo Ball as something (and I’m paraphrasing) of a circus act–slash–losing player.

Ball was coming off an expert dissection of the Dallas Mavericks: 22 points and nine assists on 8-of-14 shooting, lifting Minnesota’s record to 9-3 overall and 6-2 since Anthony Edwards underwent knee surgery. For a Ball backer of any stripe, it was a good day to claim victory—and send up critics who couldn’t see past the wayward one-legged 3s.

Huh, I thought. I’ve always been fairly bullish on Ball? Five years ago (!) on a now-defunct ESPN show called The Jump, the host that day, my pal Cassidy Hubbarth, asked Kendrick Perkins and me to pick which ascendant point guard we’d rather have for the next five years: Ball or Ja Morant. To Perk’s mild surprise, I chose Ball. I said something that day that I’d reiterate dozens of times in defense of one of the most polarizing players in sports: The lowlights might be borderline grotesque, anathema to old-school sensibilities, but it was very rare to find Ball’s combination of size (6-foot-7), passing vision, and off-the-bounce 3-point shooting in one package. If forced to choose, I’d bet on that.

For a while, Morant (and Ball and the Charlotte Hornets) made that look like the wrong pick. Then, things happened, and it flipped.

Flash forward to today, and Ball’s shocking trade this past summer from Charlotte to the Minnesota Timberwolves has sparked an across-the-board emotional reaction unusual in its breadth, speed, and all-out ferocity. Part of one fan base is enraged. Every night—hell, every shot—is somehow a referendum on Ball, media ethics, the sport itself. How did we get here so fast?
